Short answer: In modern unified-memory GPUs, bandwidth-bound decoding latency is governed by how well the attention engine can keep the high-bandwidth memory subsystem (HBM/LPDDR5X) and the on-chip caches (L1/L2/shared) saturated with contiguous, predictable memory accesses. Hybrid linear attention and full attention differ in their memory access patterns; the former is far more cache-friendly and latency-predictable, while the latter is bandwidth- and capacity-bound.
